Still lines,small appetites

Sand on a vibrating plate collects where the plate stands still. Here each grain is a letter. In silence the grains spell a word; under sound they leave it for the plate's nodal lines, solved from the plate equation itself.

Below the plate, swimmers grow, turn round, sprout streamers and feed them, peck by peck, to the pellets that made them.

A free square plate, Poisson ratio 0.3, solved by Rayleigh-Ritz on a Legendre basis. The numbers are Leissa's frequency parameter, so you can check them against the published table.

2

02Small appetites

Swimmers feed on a dissolved pool and grow. At a set mass they turn round and grow two streamers. A grown swimmer that meets a pellet pecks it; every peck moves streamer into the pellet until the swimmer is taken in whole. Pellets leak back into the pool, bud new swimmers and divide.

Mass is conserved, so nothing here runs away. Click to drop food. It costs the pool what it gives the pellet: your attention feeds the colony and starves the water.

A word becomes a field of cells inside the construction that sizes it. The rectangle is cut by the golden ratio nine times; a quarter arc in each square makes the spiral, and a bright head runs it inward, one quarter every 1.65 seconds. Points on the letters carry their own coordinates.

Equal time per quarter Equal speed Next quarter
Save a 3840 px still Save a 16-bit PNG

Two states, one beat

An electron in hydrogen held in two states at once. Their energies differ, so the cloud sloshes between them once every 2.19 femtoseconds; here, once every 7.2 seconds. Every point rides the probability current, which keeps the cloud true to the wavefunction at every instant. Each point takes the colour of the state that carries more of the density there.

1s + 2p 2s + 3d 3s + 4f 4f + 5g 5g + 6g
Start of the beat Half a beat later
Save a 3840 px still

Bits apart

Every tile counts the bits in which two numbers differ: its column, shifted by the code of the letter it sits in, and its row. Fewer differing bits, a larger tile. Each letter carries its own field, so a word is drawn by its own character codes, and the field runs on, faint, between the letters.

“The purpose of computing is insight, not numbers.”

Every piece gets one word and a credit line that names what it is about. Built pieces link out. The rest are sounds that exist and exhibits still to make.

    The title system

    The channel we studied names a beat with the artists whose sound it wears, then one word. We keep the shape and turn it around. The line names the families the piece is about, then says what it is: an original type piece. The word is short and concrete.

A WebAudio engine in our own code, with no dependencies. Synthesis voices, tape and vinyl, bitcrush, sidechain, a swing sequencer, archival sound and nine sonic motifs. One sound for each family in the map, and five for the inner signal: thought, trauma, pain, longing and memory. Each is a module in sound/motifs/.

Type as a material

On the element table, type is a material like ink and paper. Build Color measures, converts, compares and transforms digital color: perceptual spaces, HDR tone maps, appearance models, chromatic adaptation, spectral tools, gamut mapping, ICC profiles and LUTs, with an optional GUI. build-color 1.0.2 · fair-source (FSL-1.1-
items.body_html:
Why perceptual spaces

Hex codes store raw numbers, so two colors with close hex values can look clearly different, and the reverse. Build Color also works in spaces built to track vision: CIELAB and the Oklab family space colors so equal numeric steps look equally different, CIECAM-style models account for surroundings, and JzAzBz and ICtCp handle bright HDR images.

Examples

Output from build-color 1.0.1.

Exhibit I one color in several spaces
$ build-color info ff6030
Color: #ff6030 sRGB: (1.0000, 0.3765, 0.1882) XYZ: (0.4596, 0.2985, 0.0614) Lab (D65): (61.52, 58.31, 56.98) Oklab: (0.6128, 0.8175, 0.0611) Oklch: (0.6128, 0.8198, 4.3) Luminance: 0.2984 Dominant wavelength: 775 nm Contrast vs white: 3.01:1 vs black: 6.97:1

Lightness, chroma, hue, luminance, dominant wavelength and text contrast against white and black, with D65 as the reference white.

Exhibit II five color-difference metrics
$ build-color difference ff0000 00ff00 --metric all
Color 1: #ff0000 Color 2: #00ff00 CIE76 170.1404 CIE94 74.8681 CIEDE2000 87.6784 CMC(2:1) 104.2193 HyAB 201.1010

Red against green under CIE76, CIE94, CIEDE2000, CMC and HyAB. The metrics disagree, so --metric all shows every one.

Exhibit III a triadic scheme in a perceptual space
$ build-color harmony ff6030 --scheme triadic
Base: #ff6030 Scheme: triadic 1. #ff6030 (1.000, 0.376, 0.188) 2. #588a00 (0.349, 0.543, 0.000) 3. #fe51ff (0.999, 0.320, 1.000)

Three colors spaced evenly in a perceptual space, so they look evenly apart.

Other commands: convert between any two spaces, spectrum for a color from a color temperature, and icc to write a display profile. Run build-color with no arguments for the GUI.

Spaces, tone maps and metrics

Spaces: sRGB, Linear RGB, XYZ, xyY, CIELAB, LCH, Oklab, Oklch, JzAzBz, JzCzhz, ICtCp, HSV, Display P3, BT.2020, Adobe RGB, ACEScg. HDR tone mapping: ACES (Narkowicz + Hill), AgX (neutral / punchy / golden), Reinhard, Hable/Uncharted 2, Lottes, Uchimura/Gran Turismo, PBR Neutral (Khronos glTF), BT.2390 EETF, BT.2446 Method A, and a custom knee. Difference by CIE76, CIE94, CIEDE2000, CMC, HyAB; chromatic adaptation, color-blindness simulation, gamut mapping, color naming, 3D-LUT I/O.

build-color 1.0.2 is on PyPI under FSL-1.1-MIT (each release converts to MIT after two years) and runs on Python 3.10 or newer. It works on digital color values; measuring a physical screen needs a calibrated instrument.

Install and run it

Python 3.10 or newer.

$ pip install build-color
$ build-color info ff6030 # every space for one color
$ build-color convert ff6030 --to oklab
$ build-color difference ff0000 00ff00 --metric all
$ build-color # or launch the GUI

What counts as a splat.

The acceptance boundary is intentionally stricter than visual resemblance.

A scene artifact exists.

The result must include a loadable spatial file: an .ngsf model with a SHA-256 receipt, checked before the scene draws. A PNG, video, or still render alone is not the scene.

The camera changes the evidence.

Translation must produce meaningful parallax, changing occlusion, and a different spatial relationship among visible elements.

The source remains visible.

The original artwork stays canonical and is shown beside the generated scene. The experiment does not overwrite or silently “upgrade” it.

The invention is disclosed.

The record must identify the generator commit, provider and model versions, parameters, output hash, and inferred backsides, holes, floating fragments, or duplicated forms.

Current boundary.

Source selection and receipts are complete. Scene generation is not.

No Gaussian-splat scene is being represented as finished on this page. The three source PNGs and their hashes are prepared. The generation route is now this repository's own native pipeline: the hybrid renderer and the certified world-package contract in system/spatial-scene.js and system/engine/world-package.js, with no hosted model, no credentials, and no metered endpoint. A single-image result will be described as a generated spatial interpretation, not a scan or measured reconstruction. Both lanes already run in the Studio's Spatial source: the reconstruction lane serves the session's Crystal City hybrid scene (a generated spatial interpretation of one canonical artwork, its invented support fill labeled), and the authored lane serves a world whose every primitive is generated from a named seed. These three pilot sources remain unreconstructed until each has its own composition profile, and each lane is labeled as what it is.
27 atlas scenes held back

The Spatial Atlas holds 27 .ngsf scenes, one per canonical artwork, each with a SHA-256 receipt, parallax that reorders up to 65% of splat pairs at the camera limits, and its source beside it. Their files are byte-identical to a fresh extraction from the Native Gaussian Splat Atlas v0.5.0 build they came from. The code that trained them is known only as version 0.5.0: no commit and no code hash survives. The disclosure line asks for the generator commit, so none of the 27 is published here. They stay viewable as spatial studies in the Studio's Spatial source.

Superframe

Superframe is the core of The Playground. Describe a piece in plain words and get it back in every medium at once: a painting, a page of living type, a line drawing, a carved material, a sound and a touch pattern, all from one seeded recipe. Then read it back as a study of its own parts, in whichever sense works for you.

Version
0.3.0
Runs on
Node 24 or later, no dependencies
Licence
FSL-1.1-MIT; fonts under the SIL Open Font License 1.1
Source
HarperZ9/superframe
PaintLinesTypeMaterial

One recipe, four of its six readouts. Each one sweeps in as a front from where its strongest element sits; choose one to hold it.

Try it

git clone https://github.com/HarperZ9/superframe
cd superframe
npm run make -- "heavy rust coral upper left, fine teal frost on the right" out/first --seed first

The same words and seed give the same files, byte for byte. Change one word and only that element changes, in every medium, in the same place. Text in quotes inside the description becomes the type.

One recipe, every medium

This piece came from one sentence. Each surface on this site stands in as the law that shares its property: the gallery's seeded plates as a tiling, the Studio's timeline as poured ink, Night School's paths as a mycelium network, the explainers as contour lines, the fractal suite as Turing coral, transparency as frost. The type sets the line "properties and laws, back to one".

Hear it

Left to right is time, top to bottom is pitch. The coral in the upper left plays early and high, and the ochre network plays late and low.

Sixteen seconds of the same piece as sound: 72 partials from 70 Hz to 7 kHz, each one's loudness read from a band of the picture.

The piece as its own study

Every render can draw a study plate from its own data. The graph joins each element to each medium, and an edge's width is how much of the element survived the crossing, measured from the outputs. The strip below it is the sound, drawn back as a spectrogram: the picture again, read as a score.

Hear an image, see a sound

Every element is a law acting on a field: reaction-diffusion coral, marbling, frost, ink in a fluid, a slime-mould network, Kepler orbits and nine more. Each medium reads that field its own way, and the mapping is fixed and stated, so a person can learn to hear where things are and to see what a sound holds. You pick the readout that works for you, or layer two. The engine's room opens a private local space for this, where words, numbers, pictures and sound turn into one another. It is a creative tool, and it makes no claims about therapy or outcomes.

A study for every reader

Each render writes a study of its own parts. study.md gives one plain sentence per element and alt text for each medium, for people and screen readers. study.json gives the properties, the weights each law read and the ones it ignored, and a measured record of how much of each element survived into each medium, for software and language models. tactile.json is a vibration pattern for a phone.

Change it freely

node superframe/cli/superframe.mjs artifact out/first/recipe.json out/b --isomer permute
node superframe/cli/superframe.mjs artifact out/first/recipe.json out/c --metamer coral
node superframe/cli/superframe.mjs artifact out/first/recipe.json out/d --route coral:sound:0
Isomer
the same weights in a new arrangement
Metamer
an ink that matches in daylight and splits under tungsten
Route
how much of an element passes into a medium; 0 silences it there
Edit
one weight, by its path in the recipe

What is tested

271 tests run with npm test. The same recipe repeats byte for byte in every medium. A one-weight edit changed 37,122 paint pixels inside its element's region and none outside, and no sound outside its time window. The same check after a global step finds 186,861 pixels outside, so it can fail. A word the reader does not know changes nothing.

Limits

  • Each law runs on its own grid, a few hundred cells across its region, so up close its edges are soft. This piece renders at full 4K size in about 35 seconds.
  • Elements do not act on one another yet; each law runs alone in its region.
  • Type is the weakest crossing: on this piece an element's ticks correlate with what the type shows at 0.06 to 0.33, against up to 0.80 for paint, 0.87 for sound and 0.94 for material.
  • The intent reader knows a small English vocabulary. Words it does not know are listed, never guessed.

items.body_html:
Flywheel

Flywheel: Run any model, and check its answer before you rely on it.

Flywheel runs AI tasks with the model you choose and checks each answer against the record it came from. A wrong answer is held before your team acts on it.

The baron's trick

The baron said he pulled himself out of the swamp by his own hair. A model that grades its own answer tells the same story, and it tells it with a straight face.

So Flywheel never lets the model accept itself. A check outside the model, a test run or a source comparison, decides. The model proposes; the record disposes.1

The baron's room

  1. 1. The regress has a name: the Münchhausen trilemma, from Hans Albert, Treatise on Critical Reason, 1968. Every justification ends in a circle, an endless regress or a stop by decree. Back to the text

The record says 41

41

Says 42, names the record Says 41, names the record Says 41, names nothing

tests_passed: 42, source: the test record

Fail, held

The value disagrees with the record.

tests_passed: 41, source: the test record

Pass, released

The value agrees with the record.

tests_passed: 41, no source

Unverifiable, held

The value agrees, and the answer does not say where it came from.

Run the three checks

How an answer gets accepted

  1. Model proposesCheap, replaceable, asked for more when needed.
  2. Outside checkNo learned model here. It accepts or rejects.
  3. ReceiptNamed by its own fingerprint; re-check it offline.
  4. Stronger tierNamed when the budget runs out. You decide.
  5. Proof cacheRe-checked before it is served again.

Same check, two hands

In yours

A green tick you can take apart: the record, the check and the receipt.

In the wrong ones

A green tick that launders a false result.

What keeps it in yours: the check runs outside the model, the checker never certifies itself, and a corpus of known false answers tests the checker on every release.

Install it

The core package needs only the Python standard library. Use hosted models with your keys, or run offline against local weights. Source on GitHub.

pip install flywheel-verify
flywheel up

items.body_html:
Pulled out by his own hair

In Raspe's tales the baron hauls himself and his horse out of a swamp by his own hair.1 Philosophy kept the image for a problem with no easy floor: ask why a claim holds, then ask again, and you end in one of three places. They hang in this room.

The three horns

  1. The circle

    The reason leans on the thing it was meant to prove. A model grading its own answer lives here.

  2. RECEIPT 1: the answer is rightRECEIPT 2: receipt 1 is rightRECEIPT 3: receipt 2 is rightRECEIPT 4: receipt 3 is right ...

    The regress

    Every check needs a check. The paper never runs out, and nothing is ever settled.

  3. Accepted

    The decree

    Someone stops the questions by authority. The stamp is real; the reason behind it is not on the page.

Stand on the record

Albert's own answer was to keep every result open to criticism, never to finish the proof.2 That is the floor Flywheel builds on. The check sits outside the model, against a record the model did not write, and anyone can run it again.

It does not escape the trilemma. It makes the stopping point visible and re-runnable, which is the most a check can honestly offer.

Show me

Three answers against one record, and what the checker decided: the Flywheel room.

  1. 1. Rudolf Erich Raspe, Baron Munchausen's Narrative of his Marvellous Travels and Campaigns in Russia, 1785. The slab behind the title is Gustave Doré's 1862 bust of the baron, public domain. Back to the text
  2. 2. Hans Albert, Treatise on Critical Reason, 1968, which names the trilemma and argues for critical testing in its place. Back to the text

The world

Seven strata, from the surface down: material, property, process, form, composition, rules, meaning.

Bridges

  • Tile: The unit that carries one piece of the whole: Olivetti's blocks and ribbon tiles, Byzantine tesserae, Martens' glyph cells, a story beat in a sequence. Joins mosaic (form), tessellation (process), glyph cell (form), grid (form), reading order (composition).
  • Thread: A line that joins: a sewing thread, a network edge, a rope strand, a ribbon. Joins weaving stitching (process), network graph (form), line hatching (form), ribbon (form).
  • Sheet: A translucent layer: Pink Noise's acetate, an overprint ink, a depth plane, a sound layer under a kick. Joins layering (process), opacity (property), overprint (process), plane sheet (form), depth planes (composition).
  • Grain: The small random texture of a medium: paper tooth, film grain, pigment granulation, the noise floor. Joins grain texture (property), error as texture (meaning), noise as signal (meaning), film stock (material), paper (material).
  • Grid of time: Time laid out as cells: a contact sheet, a temporal mosaic, a 30desk wall of timed studies, numbered steps. Joins time as material (meaning), tessellation (process), held frames timing (process), reading order (composition).
  • Stroke: One continuous mark carried by a hand or a flow: a brush spiral, a burin cut, a one-stroke dragon, a letter's skeleton. Joins path stroke (form), advection (process), viscosity (property), line hatching (form), type (material).
  • Front: The moving edge between two states: an ink-bloom reveal, a style infection across a grid, a wave front, a burn line. Joins advection (process), diffusion (process), erosion (process), transformation (process).
  • Ring: A closed loop that spreads or holds: a ripple, a drum's nodal circle, an iris, a halo. Joins ring orbit (form), wave form (form), resonance pitch (property), aperture eye (form).
  • Window: An opening that frames and bends what is seen: Snell's window, the eye, a frame within a frame, a grey rectangle in a flower. Joins aperture eye (form), refraction (property), framing (composition), light (material).
  • Tide line: The dark edge left where a liquid stops: a soak-stain rim, an ink bloom's edge, a beach's wrack line, sediment in the medium. Joins sedimentation (process), bleed (process), water (material), pigment (material), absorbency (property).
  • Glint: A single bright reflection from a tilted facet: sun glitter on waves, a highlight on glass, a specular dot. Joins gloss reflectance (property), light (material), water (material), wave form (form).
  • Drop: A unit of liquid added to a medium: a pigment drop, an ink drop in water, a raindrop, a kick that ducks the pad. Joins diffusion (process), surface tension (property), water (material), ink (material), pigment (material).
  • Joint: The cut between parts that lets a whole be taken apart and rebuilt: an I-beam mark between premises, a grout line between tesserae, a cut in a recut film, a seam in a parts tree. Joins decomposition measure (process), argument structure (process), tessellation (process), collage recut (process).

Rules

  • Composition: Foreground frames, midground holds the character and focal point, background sets the scene; each plane has one job.
  • Composition: Horizon placement and mass size make or break a vertical frame; a 50/50 split is a hard sell and equal masses feel the same.
  • Composition: Pattern colour temperature at the macro level (cool sky, warm ground) and alternate it at the micro level; put red in foliage shadows.
  • Composition: Neutral pose, camera and background connect to a character; dynamic ones build tension; mixing them carelessly causes dissonance.
  • Craft: Readability is king: contrast serves separation and the focal point before poetry.
  • Canon: One hot mark per view; colour is verdict-only in UI.
  • Canon: No taglines, helper text or secondary labels; if a screen needs them, redesign it.
  • Canon: Two type families only, one grotesk and one mono; hierarchy from weight and size.
  • Canon: Break every reference into parts and recombine them into our own system; never copy piecewise.
  • Craft: Tesserae are laid in courses (andamento) that follow the form's contour, so the flow of the tiles describes the shape.
  • Craft: Erosion should follow local stroke width so thin parts of a letter survive.
  • Craft: In intaglio, tone comes from line density and width under a raking light, never from flat fill; the edge exists where cuts end.
  • Craft: Fix the time (a 30-minute lock) so the study gets finished; the time becomes part of the work ('Done in mm:ss').
  • Craft: Physical imperfection (ink spread, paper grain, registration error) makes motion feel alive.
  • Physical: A dye spreads with radius growing as the square root of time (r ~ t^0.5); a moving front grows linearly.
  • Physical: Evaporating liquid carries suspended pigment to the drying edge and leaves it there as a rim.
  • Physical: Overlapping transparent inks multiply their transmissions; real inks absorb outside their band, so the ideal multiply misses hue.
  • Physical: Light through a medium falls off exponentially with depth, red first in water.
  • Physical: Light bends at an interface by the ratio of refractive indices; from under water the sky shows as a window of half-angle 48.6 degrees.
  • Physical: A shape sets its resonances, but the resonances do not always fix the shape (Kac 1966; Gordon, Webb and Wolpert 1992).
  • Physical: A thin layer reflects colours that interfere constructively at its thickness; the hue walks with thickness and angle.
  • Physical: A yield-stress paint flows only where pushed past its yield value and holds ridges elsewhere.
  • Music: Keep the third thin or absent; the minor colour comes from a fifth plus a flat sixth.
  • Music: Make the flat sixth (bVI, or b6 over the pedal) the main colour move; lead cells repeat one colour tone (5, b6 or 9).
  • Music: The pad dips about 6 dB under each kick (5.9 dB on 92% of kicks in Stolie): separation by ducking.
  • Music: The room is a dark 1 to 2 s space with one wide return; harmony low-passed under about 1 kHz with slow attacks; drums carry the only brightness.

items.body_html:
The road

Ink

A drop lands and soaks outward; its ring grows as the square root of time.

Listen Lift

Ink in water

Ink floated on water keeps every turn of the current; marbled paper is that water, lifted off.

Listen Lift

Layers of water

Ground, current, picture and count, printed one over another; lift them to see each one.

Listen Lift

Tide line

Where a liquid stops, it leaves its edge behind: a soak stain's rim, a bloom's border, the wrack on a beach.

Listen Lift

Palimpsest

Water washed the first text off the leaf; the trace stayed under the new one.

Enter Sound Tile Sheet Front The map Index
Listen Lift

Light

Earth from six billion kilometres: less than one pixel, caught in a scattered sunbeam inside the camera.

Listen Lift

Refraction

Light bends where it enters water; from below, the whole sky squeezes into a circle about 97 degrees across.

Listen Lift

Thin film

A soap film a few hundred nanometres thick reflects the colours that meet in step at its thickness; as it drains, the colours walk.

Listen Lift

Window

An opening that frames and bends what is seen: the eye, a telescope's dish, a frame within a frame.

Listen Lift

Glint

Each flash on the water is one small facet tilted just right between the sun and the eye.

Afterimage Ebbinghaus Mirror Glint The map
Listen Lift

Type

Rub-down letters on a carrier sheet: one face in many sizes, hierarchy from weight and size alone.

Listen Lift

Engraving

In intaglio the tone is the lines: more and wider cuts make it darker, and there is no flat fill to lean on.

Listen Lift

Erosion

Wear a letter evenly and its hairlines go first; wear it by its own stroke width and the thin parts survive.

Listen Lift

Stroke

One continuous mark carried by a hand or a flow: a brush spiral, a burin cut, a line of thick paint that holds its ridges.

Listen Lift

Grain

Paper tooth, a worn sort, an uneven inking: the small noise of a medium is part of what it says.

Letter Scripture Grain Stroke The map
Listen Lift

Mosaic

Tesserae laid in courses that follow the form: the flow of the tiles draws the shape before the colour does.

Listen Lift

Halftone

Tone from dots of one ink: bigger dots read darker, and a slipped second screen leaves the moirÃ© that says it was printed.

Listen Lift

Tile

The unit that carries one piece of the whole: a ribbon tile, a tessera, a glyph cell, one beat of a story.

Listen Lift

Joint

The cut between parts lets a whole be taken apart and rebuilt: a grout line, a seam, the turn between premises in an argument.

Listen Lift

Grid

A grid holds every cell equal until one mark turns hot; then the eye goes there first.

Labels Lossy Static Joint The map
Listen Lift

Sound

Berliner's gramophone cut sound as a groove in a flat disc; a room's echo is the sound still arriving after it stops.

Listen Lift

Resonance

Sand on a bowed plate gathers on the lines that stay still; each pitch draws its own figure.

Listen Lift

The pad ducks

Two bars of the theme: the pad dips under every kick, so the two never cover each other.

Listen Lift

Ring

A closed loop that spreads or holds: a ripple, a drum's nodal circle, an iris, a halo.

Listen Lift

The cycle

The theme turns on the flat sixth: the tonic, then the sixth over the same low note, again and again.

Listen Groove Lullaby Anempathetic Ring
Listen Lift

Ticker

Edison's ticker printed prices on paper tape as they arrived: data as a ribbon, read in order.

Listen Lift

Telegraph

A key, a code and a wire: every message cut into marks and spaces before it could travel.

Listen Lift

Grid of time

Time laid out as cells: a contact sheet, a timed study, a fixed half hour that makes the work finish.

Listen Lift

Switchboard

An operator joins any line to any other by hand; the tools here do that work for checks, words, sources and code.

Flywheel Articulate Daylight BuildLang raw-native
Listen Lift

Redaction

A redacted page shows exactly where something was taken out; the black bar is a record too.

Listen Lift

Argument

Split a claim into premises, presuppositions and a conclusion, and every 'so' and 'but' becomes a turn you can check.

Listen Lift

Thread

A line that joins: a sewing thread, a network edge, a rope strand; here, every bridge in the world drawn between its places.

Listen Lift

The weighing

In the Papyrus of Hunefer the heart is weighed against a feather and a scribe writes the result down: a check, with a record.
